key_insight: SJ-KAN propagates spatial derivatives analytically through a compact spectral network, achieving comparable or better accuracy than PINN and PIKAN baselines with substantially lower computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make physics-informed incompressible flow simulation more affordable, including high-Reynolds-number cavity flows without reference data.
method: Embed coordinates in Chebyshev bases and precompute basis derivatives at collocation points.
Compress the bases linearly into latent features, then map them to physical variables with one nonlinear Chebyshev KAN layer.
Evaluate PDE derivatives analytically; use automatic differentiation only for loss gradients with respect to weights.
evidence_signal: Tests on the Taylor–Green vortex and lid-driven cavity at Re = 100–10,000 report up to 47× fewer parameters and 8.2× faster training per epoch than the baselines; the Re = 10,000 cavity was solved without reference data using fewer than 9,000 parameters.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish performance on complex geometries or turbulent flows, and faster epochs do not necessarily imply shorter time to convergence.
paper_title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
